source_en: Coming down from the mountain ridge for a few days.
Returning to the lower parish to check the records.
Here to drop a manuscript at the printing office.
Down from the ridge. Walked the fence looking for my dog.
Visiting the parish archive on the east side.
Looking for someone who has not answered my letters.
Returning to find my dog.
Back from the summit. I saw the lights from there and came down.
From the eastern slope. Leaving food at the east gate again.
Taking my wife to the cinema for our anniversary.
Moving to a flat in the city. I cannot stand the quiet.
Signing copies of my bestselling novel at the bookshop.
Buying a puppy. I have never kept a dog before.
Reading my poems at the Writers' Union gala tonight.
Starting work at the radio station. I like to talk.
My dog is safe at home. Just buying cigarettes.
I have stopped writing. Selling my pens at the market.
Returning to the city parish I have served for twenty years.
I had the dog with me last time. He is at home tonight.
The mountain road was clear. First time in a while.
Here. My papers are in order.
My dog ran off last week. I keep checking the perimeter fence on the way in.
Quieter down here than I expected. That is not a comfort.
I have been writing more than usual. The words come easier when things are wrong.
If a large grey dog comes through this gate, hold him. That is mine.
I am not here for anything except the dog.
The manuscript is finished. I do not know what that means yet.
Thank you. This won't take long.
If you see my dog near the east gate, hold him for me.
I'll be out of your way.
Fine. I'll wait. I have nowhere pressing to be.
You think this matters to me. I've been in worse rooms.
Doesn't matter. I have nothing to get back to.
I had more of the manuscript left. That's all.
The dog would have found me eventually. Now it doesn't matter.
Let it be quiet.
A cell is still quieter than you'd think. I've worked in worse silence.
At least in isolation, no one else can ruin the quiet.
If they give me something to write with, I'll use the wall.
I always wondered what God was thinking when He made me. Now I'll know.
Every poem ends. Most just end badly.
They were His words anyway. Not mine. I was only ever the hand.
Where are you coming from?
The parish above the north ridge. The road down was clear for once. The dog stayed home.
The ridge. I walked the perimeter fence on the way down. My dog ran off last week. I keep looking.
The eastern slope. I left food by the east gate again. He has not come for it.
My flat behind the bread factory. I have lived in town all my life. The mountain is for people with more patience.
From my wife's house. She keeps it warm. She never minded the quiet up there, not like people say.
From the parish. The dog walked down with me, as always. He is waiting by your gate now.
Are you experiencing any symptoms?
I sleep poorly. I always have. Otherwise, no.
I hear things at night. The wind through the pass, probably. I write until it stops.
A heaviness in the hands. I write through it. The words come anyway. They always come.
None. I sleep like a child. Always have. Nothing in this world keeps me awake.
No complaints. I have stopped writing entirely, so I sleep. The nights are empty and restful.
Nothing. I am barely thirty. The body keeps up with me on the mountain.
I had the dog with me last time. He is at home tonight.
I write when I cannot sleep. Lately I cannot sleep very much.
Quiet suits me. I don't say that as a complaint.
My dog has been gone for nearly two weeks. I don't know where he went.
I have been writing more than usual. There is nothing else to do in the quiet.
The mountain has changed. Something about the way it sits now.
If you see a large grey dog near the perimeter fence, that is mine. He would not have gone far on his own.
I have been leaving food outside the east gate. He has not come.
The words don't come from me. They never did. I was only ever the hand holding the pen.
